speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what is the current number and percentage of Singaporeans who are on the various public transport concession schemes and how do the figures compare to those five years ago; (b) whether there are assessments done on the number of Singaporeans, especially senior citizens, who are likely to be on the concession scheme by 2020 and 2030 as a result of our ageing population; and (c) whether the senior citizens concession scheme has resulted in more travels by senior citizens.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: These include students, full-time National Servicemen and senior citizens.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We have also recently included persons with disabilities and Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) beneficiaries to the concessions framework in 2014.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This suggests that senior citizens are making more trips, which could be due to reasons other than the concession.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The concessions formula was also reviewed in 2012/2013.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Will there be a review soon to keep up with the changing needs?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The other thing is, with the increase in the number, how are the fare concessions funded?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Because with the numbers, can the current funding model continue to fund when the number of seniors or the people on concession increase substantially?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Will there be enhancements soon, especially for the Workfare Supplement scheme?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The concession schemes are decided by the Public Transport Council (PTC) and reviewed by it regularly.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, PTC will ensure that our public transport fares remain affordable.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Of course, besides the low-income groups, there will be other segments of the population that require support.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: And PTC will continue to review and, if necessary, enhance the concession schemes to take care of these various groups, including senior citizens, students and persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Miss Cheng is right that there is cost to these concessions.
